title: Most Adults Cannot Pass This Surgeon's Entrance Exam
summary: Explore Anatomy and Safety, Checks and Approaches, Structures and Tools, Monitoring and Recovery, People and Decisions across five six-question rounds.

landing.intro:
Precision starts with knowledge.
How well can you connect the clues?

about.body:
Five rounds offer different angles on this challenge: Anatomy and Safety, Checks and Approaches, Structures and Tools, Monitoring and Recovery, People and Decisions. Each round contains six distinct questions.

Choose one of four answers and move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. The target is 24 correct answers out of 30. The result describes this quiz attempt only.

For entertainment and general learning only. This is not a medical-school admission exam, surgical qualification, diagnosis or medical advice. Seek qualified medical care for personal symptoms, wound concerns or emergencies.

steps: Press Start, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question and progress through five rounds.
Complete all 30 questions to reveal your result. You can then unlock the full breakdown.

surgeon-q1.question: In the circulatory system, what defines an artery?

answers.a1: It carries blood away from the heart
answers.a3: It carries blood only to the lungs

surgeon-q2.question: What is the main purpose of maintaining a sterile surgical field?

answers.a1: To keep instruments arranged by size
answers.a2: To reduce contamination and the risk of infection
answers.a3: To make the procedure finish faster

surgeon-round1-new1.question: Which tissue connects a muscle to a bone?

answers.a1: Tendon
A surgical cut

surgeon-round1-new3.question: What is the main purpose of checking a patient's identity before a procedure?

answers.a1: To ensure care is intended for the correct person
answers.a2: To determine the patient's pain tolerance
answers.a3: To replace all other safety checks

surgeon-round1-new4.question: Why should a surgical team confirm relevant allergies?

answers.a1: To reduce the risk of an avoidable reaction
answers.a3: To prove all medicines are safe

surgeon-q3.question: What should a surgical safety pause immediately before an incision confirm?

answers.a1: Only the expected procedure length
answers.a3: The correct patient, procedure and body site
answers.a4: The patient's meal choice after surgery

surgeon-q4.question: What makes laparoscopic surgery different from a traditional open approach?

answers.a1: It never requires pain control
answers.a3: It can only examine the skin
answers.a4: It commonly uses a camera and instruments through small incisions

answers.a1: An approach designed to limit the size of access openings or tissue disruption
answers.a2: A procedure with no possible risks
answers.a4: A procedure that never needs anaesthesia

surgeon-round2-new2.question: What is a suture commonly used for?

answers.a1: Holding tissues together
Removal of a sample for examination
Before an operation

surgeon-q5.question: Which structure is removed during an appendectomy?

answers.a1: The appendix

surgeon-q6.question: What is a surgical retractor mainly used for?

answers.a1: Measuring oxygen saturation
answers.a2: Holding tissue or an incision open to improve access

answers.a1: Gallbladder

surgeon-round3-new2.question: What does a vein generally do?

answers.a1: Carries blood toward the heart
answers.a3: Always carries blood away from the heart

answers.a1: Stopping or controlling bleeding

surgeon-round3-new4.question: What does a surgical specimen label need to support?

answers.a1: Correct identification of the patient and specimen

surgeon-q7.question: Which combination can suggest a surgical-site infection?

answers.a1: Improving comfort and a dry healing wound
answers.a2: A steady appetite and normal temperature
answers.a3: Increasing redness or pain, drainage, or fever
answers.a4: A clean dressing with no new symptoms

surgeon-q8.question: Which device gives a rapid, non-invasive estimate of blood oxygen saturation during surgery?

answers.a1: Reflex hammer

surgeon-round4-new1.question: Why count relevant instruments and materials during surgery?

answers.a1: To help prevent unintentionally retained items
answers.a4: To decide whether consent was needed

surgeon-round4-new2.question: What does postoperative monitoring help identify?

answers.a1: Changes in recovery that may need assessment

surgeon-round4-new3.question: Which term describes separation of a previously closed wound?

answers.a1: Wound dehiscence
A collection of blood outside blood vessels

surgeon-q9.question: A person becomes unresponsive and is not breathing normally. What is the safest immediate general response?

answers.a1: Call emergency services and begin appropriate basic life support

surgeon-q10.question: Which description best matches informed consent before surgery?

answers.a1: The clinician chooses without explaining alternatives
answers.a2: The patient receives relevant information and agrees voluntarily
answers.a3: A relative always decides for every adult
answers.a4: Signing a form removes the need for discussion

surgeon-round5-new1.question: What should a team member do if an important safety check appears incomplete?

answers.a1: Speak up and seek clarification before proceeding
answers.a4: Wait until the patient has left

surgeon-round5-new2.question: Why discuss alternatives when obtaining consent?

answers.a1: To help the patient make an informed choice

surgeon-round5-new3.question: What is a clinical handover intended to transfer?

answers.a1: Relevant information and responsibility for continuing care

surgeon-round5-new4.question: Why are discharge instructions tailored to the procedure and patient?

answers.a1: Recovery needs and warning signs can differ
answers.a4: Every symptom after surgery is harmless
